claims.note: Replace sets every selected station, and all its sprinklers, to the entered value (SpatialAdjustLogic.cs:100-102; SpatialAdjustService.cs:2372-2383). The Replace input accepts 0-50 and defaults to 24 (sa-bulk-adjust-dlg.component.ts:68).

claims.note: Shift adds the entered value, -40 to 40 (sa-bulk-adjust-dlg.component.ts:69), to each station's own target (SpatialAdjustLogic.cs:100-102). Results are clamped to 0-50 (:104), so a station pushed past either end stops there and its difference from the others is not kept. 373-1135 rev 02 §Bulk Adjust Functionality: "Shift by -2% lowers Target VWC by 2%".

claims.text: Shift is the safer choice when the stations were individually tuned.
claims.note: Follows from bulk-adjustments/3/3: Shift keeps per-station differences, except at the 0 and 50 clamps, while Replace overwrites them. "Safer" is the guide's judgement on that basis.

claims.text: Option 2 — delta plus today’s ET, the default

The server computes it per station: target minus working VWC gives a deficit, the deficit becomes an amount of water, today’s ET adjusted by the crop coefficient is added, the daily maximum caps the total, and the result is divided by the Lynx reference amount.

evidence.ref: docs/claims/calculations.md §2.2 The chain, per station, per day

claims.note: The working VWC is today's measured average, or the model's earlier prediction when there is no scan today (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3031-3032). Three steps the sentence leaves out: the deficit in VWC points is added to the ET in millimetres one for one, with no conversion; the sum is floored at 0 and multiplied by the station's soil factor before the cap (:3036-3039); and the result is rounded to a whole percentage (:3043). Whether one VWC point should equal one millimetre is listed for the experts in docs/claims/calculations.md §12.

claims.text: Every suggestion in this column came from that chain.
claims.note: Under Option 2 the browser only looks up the server's stored suggestion by station name.

Option 1 multiplies the percent adjust Lynx currently holds by target divided by measured moisture, and rounds.

evidence.ref: docs/claims/calculations.md §3 Option 1: ratio of target to measured

claims.note: Retyped from label to behaviour. SPATIAL_ADJUST.SAVE_CHANGES "Save Changes" is the dialog's only save button, in the footer under every tab (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:49-55). On save the dialog compares three groups with their opening values: the site settings (the Calculation and Minimum Threshold tabs), the user preferences (the Preferences tab) and the Target Profiles (sa-settings-dlg.component.ts:445-468). It sends one request per changed group, all together (:203, :482-503), and closes when they finish. With nothing changed it just closes (:196-199).

claims.text: With unsaved edits, Cancel asks whether you want to exit without saving: Continue Editing takes you back, and Discard Changes closes the dialog and drops every edit.
claims.note: Retyped from label to behaviour. Cancel (STRINGS.CANCEL) runs the same change check as Save (sa-settings-dlg.component.ts:217-229). With no edits it closes at once. With edits it opens a confirmation headed SPATIAL_ADJUST.DISCARD_CHANGES "Discard changes" that asks SETTINGS_CONFIRM_DISCARD_CHANGES_PRIMARY "Are you sure you want to exit without saving changes?" (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:261-270). Its buttons are CONTINUE_EDITING "Continue Editing" and DISCARD_CHANGES "Discard changes", both shown upper-case, so the second reads "DISCARD CHANGES" on screen. Continue Editing hides the confirmation and leaves the dialog open with the edits. Discard changes closes the dialog without saving anything (:235-242; the toolbar removes the dialog on cancel, sa-main-toolbar.component.html:110).

VWC is the TurfRad moisture mean of its sprinkler, or the mean across its sprinklers for a multi-sprinkler station, and the latest scan date sits beside the name (sa-dash-table.component.ts:365-396, sa-table-card.component.html:22-25). 373-1135 rev 02 §Table Functionality: "Avg. VWC: Average of scans within the sprinkler boundary from TurfRad". On a day with no scan the figure is the model's estimate under Option 2, drawn grey and italic (see dashboard-overview/4/7), or "--" under Option 1.

claims.text: Measured moisture and its scan date, per station.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: You supply the target
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: Target VWC is the moisture you want that station to hold.
claims.note: 373-1135 rev 02 §Table Functionality: Target VWC is user-defined and can be unique for each station.

claims.text: It is yours to set, station by station, between 0 and 50 percent.
claims.note: The input takes whole numbers 0-50 (sa-table-card.component.html:40-47), and bulk changes are clamped to the same range (SpatialAdjustLogic.cs:93-105). Until the user sets one, the target starts at the station's measured VWC (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3128-3133).

claims.text: The gap between measured and target is what the calculation works on.
claims.note: Under Option 2 the gap is Target VWC minus the modelled VWC, which is the measured mean on a day with a scan (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3033). Option 1 uses the ratio of target to measured instead (sa-algorithm.service.ts:58-60).

claims.text: Target VWC is an editable input, not a reading.
claims.note: A numeric input bound to targetVwcPercent.

claims.text: Spatial Adjust does the arithmetic
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: The difference between target and measured moisture becomes an amount of water, today’s ET is added, the daily maximum caps it, and the result is divided by the Lynx reference amount to give a percentage.
claims.note: Option 2 on the server: delta = Target VWC − modelled VWC (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3033); amount = (today's ET + delta) × soil factor, floored at 0 (:3037-3039); capped at the Daily Max Amount (:3041); suggested % = capped amount ÷ Lynx Reference Amount × 100, rounded (:3043). Two details the sentence leaves out: ET is first multiplied by the Crop Coefficient (:2972-2974), and the soil factor applies only when SpatialAdjust:UseSoilFactor is on (SpatialAdjustLogic.cs:142-147). Option 1 does not use this chain.
claims.developNote: On develop (bd39f465) the same arithmetic moves into CalculateAdjustment (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3211-3232), and a new pass writes today's adjustment from the carried-forward model on days with no new scan (:3280-3325).

claims.text: The Suggested column is the output of that chain.
claims.note: Under Option 2, the default, Suggested is the server's stored value (sa-algorithm.service.ts:62-65). Under Option 1 it is Target VWC ÷ measured VWC × Lynx Current instead (:58-60).

claims.text: In one line. Suggested % = the applied amount ÷ the Lynx reference amount × 100, rounded.
claims.note: Rounded half away from zero to a whole percent.

claims.text: Lynx runs the water
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: Spatial Adjust never waters anything.
claims.note: The only Lynx write from Spatial Adjust is requestChangePercentAdjust (lynx-cloud.service.ts:80-95), called from the push service (sa-push-changes.service.ts:208). Nothing in IntelliDash starts a program or a valve.

claims.text: It writes a percent adjust value onto each station in Lynx, and Lynx applies that percentage to the station’s programmed run time.
claims.note: First half verified: the push writes one percent adjust value per station to Lynx (sa-push-changes.service.ts:208, lynx-cloud.service.ts:80-95). How Lynx applies it is Lynx-side behaviour the IntelliDash source cannot settle. 373-1135 rev 02 §Settings Configuration ties the Lynx Reference Amount to the program's Next Amt., which suggests Lynx scales an amount rather than a time.
claims.question: When Spatial Adjust writes a station's Pct Adjust to Lynx, does Lynx scale the station's programmed run time, or its programmed amount (Next Amt.) before converting that to run time?

claims.text: Nothing changes until you push.
claims.note: Read as "nothing changes in Lynx". Target VWC and % Adj. edits are saved to IntelliDash straight away (SpatialAdjustService.cs:1153-1254), but they reach the controller only through the push.

claims.text: Push Changes is the only thing that writes to the controller.
claims.note: requestChangePercentAdjust has one caller in the Spatial Adjust code, the push service (sa-push-changes.service.ts:208).

claims.text: You can name the three inputs: measured VWC, target VWC and today’s ET.
claims.note: These are the three per-station inputs under Option 2. The calculation also uses the Daily Max Amount, the Lynx Reference Amount, the Crop Coefficient and, when enabled, the station's soil factor (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2968-2974, :3036-3043). Option 1 uses measured VWC, Target VWC and the Lynx Current percentage, and no ET.

claims.text: You know that nothing reaches Lynx until Push Changes is used.
claims.note: Retyped from label to behaviour.

claims.text: Understanding VWC
claims.note: Tile title.

claims.text: Measured, modelled and target volumetric water content.
claims.note: Tile summary. Measured is today's scan mean, modelled is the Option 2 estimate for a station not scanned today, and target is the editable Target VWC.

claims.text: Three different numbers wear the label VWC.
claims.note: Avg. VWC carries either the measured or the modelled value (sa-dash-table.component.ts:365-383), and Target VWC is the third.

claims.text: Knowing which one you are reading explains most surprises.
claims.note: Editorial. The visual cue that separates the two Avg. VWC readings is covered under understanding-vwc/2/3.

claims.text: Table, Avg. VWC and Target VWC
claims.note: SPATIAL_ADJUST.AVG_VWC "Avg. VWC" and SPATIAL_ADJUST.TARGET_VWC "Target VWC" are table column headers; at area and hole level the second reads SPATIAL_ADJUST.AVG_TARGET_VWC "Avg. Target VWC".

claims.text: VWC is volumetric water content, expressed as a percentage of soil volume.
claims.note: 373-1135 rev 02 (introduction) expands VWC as "volumetric water content", and the table shows it with a % sign (sa-table-card.component.html:30), but neither the guide nor the source says what the percentage is of. The value is TurfRad's moisture_mean, passed through unchanged (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3004-3012).
claims.question: Is TurfRad's moisture_mean volumetric water content as a percentage of soil volume (water volume ÷ soil volume × 100)?

claims.text: Measured: the scan mean
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: When the scan date is today, Avg.
claims.note: Read with understanding-vwc/1/3; the sentence splitter cut "Avg. VWC" in two. See that claim's note.

claims.text: VWC is the mean moisture TurfRad measured across that station.
claims.note: A scan is current when its date is today in the site's time zone (spatial-adjust-course.model.ts:173-182, spatial-adjust.util.ts:16-19). A single-sprinkler station then shows its TurfRad moisture_mean, and a multi-sprinkler station the mean across its sprinklers (sa-dash-table.component.ts:365-383). 373-1135 rev 02 §Table Functionality: "Average of scans within the sprinkler boundary from TurfRad".

claims.text: It is a measurement, and it is the number the calculation prefers.
claims.note: The server uses the mean of today's scans when there is one and falls back to the model only when there is none (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3032).

claims.text: A current scan: black text, today’s date.
claims.note: Figure caption. A current value has no sa-vwc-estimated class, so it keeps the default text colour; the scan date beside the name is always grey (sa-table-card.component.html:24).

claims.text: Modelled: the fallback
claims.note: Step title. Option 2 only; see understanding-vwc/2/2.

claims.text: When the scan is not current, Spatial Adjust falls back to a modelled value carried forward from the last scan and the weather since.
claims.note: With no scan today the server takes the previous adjustment's predicted result as the modelled VWC (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3031-3032). That prediction is the earlier modelled VWC minus that day's crop-adjusted ET plus the water the suggestion assumed would be applied (:3042), so it carries the last scan forward through the weather and the assumed irrigation. Only under Option 2; under Option 1 nothing is modelled and the cell shows "--" (sa-table-card.component.ts:374-375).
claims.developNote: On develop (bd39f465) the same arithmetic moves into CalculateAdjustment (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3211-3232), and a new pass writes today's adjustment from the carried-forward model on days with no new scan (:3280-3325).

claims.text: It is shown in grey italics so you can tell it apart at a glance.
claims.note: On a station row the modelled value gets class sa-vwc-estimated, dark grey and italic, with a calculator icon (sa-table-card.component.html:29-31; .less:97-117). The expanded sprinkler rows of a multi-sprinkler station are not italic; a modelled sprinkler is marked by an orange calculator icon instead (sa-table-card.component.html:86-92; .less:121-130).

claims.text: Station 7AP1 has no current scan; the value shown is modelled.
claims.note: Figure caption. The station name is the figure's sample data.

claims.text: Target: your input
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: Target VWC is a whole number from 0 to 50 that you set per station.
claims.note: Numeric input with 0 decimal places, min 0, max 50 (sa-table-card.component.html:40-47). The value is stored for the station and copied to its other sprinklers (SpatialAdjustService.cs:1215-1229).

claims.text: Higher targets ask for more water.
claims.note: A higher target raises the delta, the amount and so the suggestion under Option 2 (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3033-3043), until the Daily Max Amount caps it; under Option 1 the suggestion scales with target ÷ measured (sa-algorithm.service.ts:58-60).

claims.text: It is the only VWC on the row you can type into.
claims.note: Avg. VWC is a read-only cell and Target VWC is the only VWC input. The % Adj. input on the same row is a percentage of the Lynx run, not a VWC.

claims.text: Target VWC accepts 0 to 50, integers only.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: The delta is what drives the suggestion
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: Subtract the working VWC from the target and you have the deficit the calculation must close.
claims.note: Retyped from prerequisite to calculation. Delta = Target VWC − modelled VWC (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3033), where the working VWC is today's scan mean or, without one, the modelled value. If the modelled VWC is 0 the delta is set to 0.

claims.text: Add today’s ET, cap it at the daily maximum, and express it against the Lynx reference amount.
claims.note: Amount = (ET × Crop Coefficient + delta) × soil factor, floored at 0 (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2972-2974, :3037-3039), capped at the Daily Max Amount (:3041), then ÷ Lynx Reference Amount × 100 (:3043). The sentence omits the Crop Coefficient and the optional soil factor. 373-1135 rev 02 §Settings Configuration gives the cap's effect: Daily Max 10 mm over Reference 5 mm caps the suggestion at 200%.
claims.developNote: On develop (bd39f465) the same arithmetic moves into CalculateAdjustment (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3211-3232), and a new pass writes today's adjustment from the carried-forward model on days with no new scan (:3280-3325).

claims.text: Target minus measured, per station, is the whole idea.
claims.note: Under Option 2 the difference is taken per station name, and a multi-sprinkler station shares one adjustment (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3024-3028). Option 1 uses the ratio instead (sa-algorithm.service.ts:58-60).

claims.text: Aggregate rows average their children
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: At hole and area level the same two columns show averages rather than readings, and the scan date column shows the most recent scan beneath that row.
claims.note: Hole and area rows show SPATIAL_ADJUST.AVG_VWC "Avg. VWC", SPATIAL_ADJUST.AVG_TARGET_VWC "Avg. Target VWC" and SPATIAL_ADJUST.LAST_SCAN "Last Scan" (sa-dash-table.component.html:9-13). A hole averages its sprinkler records that are current or modelled, averages targets per station name, and takes the newest scan beneath it as Last Scan (spatial-adjust-course.model.ts:72-96). An area averages its holes (:25-33).

claims.text: A grey calculator icon on a hole or area row means at least one station beneath it is modelled; the average turns grey and italic only when nothing beneath it was scanned today.
claims.note: Corrected wording, replacing the sentence the ledger marked Wrong (understanding-vwc/5/3); docs/text-corrections.md §25 gives the claimed and actual behaviour. Verified against production at the cited lines.

claims.note: Figure caption. "Average measured" includes modelled values for stations not scanned today under Option 2 (spatial-adjust-course.model.ts:73-85).

claims.text: You can tell a measured value from a modelled one without checking the date.
claims.note: Station rows: grey italic with a calculator icon when modelled. Sprinkler rows: an orange calculator icon. See understanding-vwc/2/3.

claims.note: Retyped from label to behaviour. The input max is 50 and bulk changes clamp to 50 (SpatialAdjustLogic.cs:93-105).
